characters.description: Considered to be the main character along with Max Evans. Liz is your typical girl next door. She's a beautiful human girl. The show centers around her life being saved unexpectedly by the mysterious Max Evans. She feels an instant and undeniable connection to him and realizes that he has felt the same about her from afar for years. Much of the show is dealing with the consequences of falling in love with an alien. Amicable Exes: Eventually achieves this with Kyle. Anchored Ship: Good God, Max and Liz went through almost every variety of this trope Beware the Nice Ones: Don't try to hurt Max or any of her friends and she will retaliate. Tess found this out the hard way. Brainy Brunette: Wants to be a molecular biologist.

characters.name: Max Evans
characters.description: Reserved small-town cop Max is actually aHuman Alien, but keeping his head down and maintainingThe Masqueradewas a lot easier before the love of his life came back to town and he accidentally saved her life. Almost Kiss: Several times with Liz. Angst Nuke: Max has one at the end of "Tearin' Up My Heart" (season 1 episode 3) that takes out the power for the whole city. Anti-Hero: Max's first priority is protecting his family and his secret, and he's done plenty of morally grey things in their defense. Use of his powers also affects his mental state, which doesn't help matters any. Anguished Declaration of Love: To Liz, in season 1 episode 3.

characters.name: Michael Guerin
characters.description: Michaelwasn'tadopted by the Evans and had a very difficult childhood. Though the three found each other again by age 11 and were inseparable thereafter, their different circumstances have made Michael feel resentful and Max feel guilty. As an adult he's a loner, and is much less integrated into town life than his siblings. Abusive Parents:Michael was abused by his foster father before the events of the series.The Dictatorintroduces himself to Michael and then immediately tries to murder him. When that fails, he goes straight to torture and emotional manipulation. Michael was abused by his foster father before the events of the series. The Dictatorintroduces himself to Michael and then immediately tries to murder him. When that fails, he goes straight to torture and emotional manipulation. Adaptational Sexuality: Michael was straight in the original book series and earlier TV show; here, Michael is bisexual.

characters.name: Isabel Evans
characters.description: Isabel Evans is an alien-human hybrid like her brother Max Evans and best friend Michael Guerin. She and Max were found as six-year-old children wandering in the desert by Philip and Diane Evans, who adopted them. Isabel is a very visible, popular girl at school. She hides her kind side beneath a front of haughtiness and cold unfeeling—she is the perfect, unknowable, unobtainable beauty. On the outside, she is the most outgoing of the three hybrids and blends in with the human society with ease. On the inside Isabel is probably the most vulnerable of the three. She so wants to be accepted for her alien side as much as her human side. Alpha Bitch:Subverted TropeIsabel puts on this front to protect herself and her secret, terrified of letting anyone in. She eventually lets Alex in and they fall in love. Dream Walker: Isabel's special alien ability is the ability to enter someone's dream. It's unclear if she can manipulate dreams as well. Human Alien: Although how much human and how much alien is unknown, untilWord of Godon the subject is available, and if she even has an alien form. I Just Want to Be Normal: Isabel doesn't relent on this until the last episode of the series, where the Pod Squad goes on the run from the FBI

characters.name: Alex Whitman
characters.description: Butt-Monkey:Subverted TropeAlex is left out of the loop by Maria and Liz early on and even commits a crime giving his blood to pass of as Max's without a thank you ("Blood Brother"), but Alex stands up for himself and ends his friendship with Liz briefly when she refuses to tell him the truth. Eventually Alex is let in ("Heat Wave") and becomes a part of the Pod Squad. Killed Off for Real:Tess kills him when she mindwarps him one final time after severely damaging his mind. Moment Killer: Alex has this with Isabel because of Tess, who interrupts Alex trying to ask out Isabel. ("Crazy")

characters.name: Kyle Valenti
characters.description: Actual Pacifist: Comes with the territory as a doctor. He mentions that when he was still in his internship, there was a school shooting, and the perpetrator was among the people being treated. When he asked who it was, his teacher pointedly told him it didn't matter and that his job was to treat everyone.He nearly breaks this when he finds out Jesse Manes killed his father, but decides not to go along with it in the end. Amicable Exes: With Liz. They sleep together more than once but neither wants to go further than that and though he still does harbor some feelings for her, they see each other as family. Broken Pedestal:When he realizes that his father was involved in the horrific experiments at Caulfield, he doesn't even lash out at the alien that killed him, saying that if he helped torture them, he deserved it.Rebuilt Pedestal:He learns in season 3 that his father was actually an inside man forDeep Skydoing his best to help the aliens, and was killed when this was discovered. Rebuilt Pedestal:He learns in season 3 that his father was actually an inside man forDeep Skydoing his best to help the aliens, and was killed when this was discovered. Confess in Confidence: Refuses to divulge the identity of his handprinted patient to Jesse Manes. Even when it makes investigation harder, he often refuses to divulge anything about his patients due to medical ethics.

characters.name: Sheriff Jim Valenti
characters.description: Heel–Face Turn: Starts supporting the group after Max saves his son.

characters.name: Tess Harding
characters.description: Dude Magnet: Says herself that guys are always after her and Kyle remarks on how she's hot, along with some other guys at Prom later on Everyone Loves Blondes: Kyle refers to her as a "knockout" Hands-Off Parenting: Essentially grew up without any parental restrictions – or family of any kind. Killed Off for Real:In the penultimate episode of the series, she sacrifices herself by blowing up the base with her inside. Master of Illusion: Tess's main power is to make people see what she wants them to see, hear, feel, etc. She uses this power on Alex so much that he dies as a result.

characters.name: Allies
characters.description: Sudden Sequel Death Syndrome:Killed in the first episode of Season 2. Killed Off for Real:He gets fatally injured by the Skins in Season 2, and dies in Max’s arms. The Mole:Revealed to have been working for the Kivar. Heroic Suicide:Kills herself rather than be forced to reveal Max and the others’ identities. Irrational Hatred: He despises Max before they even meet, and actually tries to kill him during their first meeting, only stopping because he is literally programmed not to.

characters.name: Government Antagonists
characters.description: Accidental Murder:Michael accidentally kills him when he uses his powers to stop Pierce from killing Valenti. Ax-Crazy: It boggles the mind that someone as blatantly psychotic, sadistic, and murder happy as Pierce made it into the FBI. Killer Cop: There is no way in hell this man should have been made a federal agent. Killed Off for Real:Michael inadvertently kills him when he uses his powers to stop Pierce from killing Valenti, and Valenti, Max, and Michael burn the body and bury it in the desert. Knight Templar: He is a deranged fanatic doggedly determined to protect Earth from aliens, and his go-to solution to people getting in his way is to either torture them or kill them.

characters.name: Alien Antagonists
characters.description: Killed Off for Real:Tess turns him into ash inadvertently while trying to mindwarp him for torturing Max. Arc Villain: For the first three episodes of Season 2. We Hardly Knew Ye:Only around for three episodes before being killed off.

characters.name: Liz Ortecho
characters.description: A biomedical researcher and daughter of undocumented Mexican immigrants. After being resurrected by Max Evans, she discovers the existence of the aliens and works to uncover the truth behind her sister’s death. Abusive Parents: Liz and Rosa's mother was emotionally abusive, pushing Liz to be perfect by withholding affection if she wasn't, driving drunk with her daughters in the car, and enabling Rosa's addictions. She outright abandoned the family when Rosa threatened to out her affair with Jim Valenti and hasn't been in contact with the family since. She finally arrives in "Como la Flor" when Arturo asks her to transfer her half of the diner to Liz so she can sponsor his residency and acts regretful of her past actions....only to reveal she was only there to steal from the safe and refuses to admit she did anything wrong, signing the papers and then leaving once she has Arturo's mother's ring. Like many abusers, she does seem to genuinely love her children, but not enough to actually care for them. Action Survivor: No combat skills, no alien superpowers, justNerves of Steel.When Wyatt tries to kill her, she startsCounting Bullets, then ambushes him while reloading. Later when he tries to burn her alive in a wooden box soaked with fuel, she waits for the fire to weaken the box and kicks her way out. Almost Kiss: Several times with Max. Amicable Exes: Liz is great friends with Kyle, her high school boyfriend, who helps her uncover the mystery throughout season 1 and who will later claim Liz asFamily of Choicein season 2. She and her ex-fiance are also on good terms.

characters.name: Isobel Evans-Bracken
characters.description: Max's twin sister Isobel seems to be one of Roswell's more prominent citizens, with a role in organizing major town events. She's primarily a telepath, though she's displayed a touch of both Max's electricity powers and Michael's telekinesis. Adaptational Sexuality: She's bisexual here but was straight in the original. The Empath: She inherited the power from her mother. She starts developing it in season 3 when she feels like her family is falling apart and starts seeking ways to mend their emotional wounds. Gay Cowboy:Gender Flippedand bisexual, but she's a queer woman with a cowboy aesthetic. Good Girls Avoid Abortion:Averted. When she finds out she's pregnant by Noah, she uses the alien serum to abort the pregnancy, nearly dying in the process. Given the strongChild by Rapeconnotations, no one blames her for it, just reprimands her for risking her life needlessly when they would have helped.

characters.name: Alex Manes
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Sergeant Manes is outright called abusive by his own son Alex, who considers losing his leg in Iraq to be less traumatic than living under his roof. At first it just seems to be general emotional abuse, as he's very controlling of his son and very disappointed when he figures out he's gay, but when he found out that Alex and Michael had sex in the toolshed, he brandished a hammer andbreaks Michael's hand with itwhen he gets in the way. Alex also says he'd tried to beat him out of being gay. Adaptational Sexuality: Alex was straight in the original book series and earlier TV show; here, he is gay. Artificial Limbs: Lost a leg in Iraq and has a prosthetic. Birds of a Feather: With Michael, They both had abusive parental figures. They both were given a better parental figure and an opportunity to live somewhere else by a family friend. For Alex it was Kyle's dad who knew his dad and gave him a cabin. For Michael it was Sanders who knew his mom and let him stay at the auto shop. They both have a love for music. They both have an affinity for science. Brutal Honesty: Outright tells Liz she’s being a bad friend to Maria.

characters.name: Maria De Luca
characters.description: Adaptation Species Change:She's human in the books. Here, she discovers she has alien ancestry. Best Friend: To Liz and Michael, as well as Rosa in high school. The Caretaker: To her mentally unwell mother. Cast from Lifespan: Her visions damage her brain. Her friends, particularly Kyle, keep trying to stop her from triggering more, but when shewitnesses a murderin season 3 she feels she has no choice but to find the truth and stop it. Locked Out of the Loop: The only one of the main cast who is completely oblivious to the supernatural. Rosa and Kyle know, while Alex has stumbled upon an alien artifact. The only clue Maria gets is her mother, who she believes is mentally unwell, talking about aliens.

characters.name: Deputy Jenna Cameron
characters.description: Badges and Dog Tags: She's an Army veteran. Friends with Benefits: With Max. Though they mutually decide to stop sleeping together, they do remain good friends. Turn in Your Badge: She's forced to resign after one too many incidents she can't explain.

characters.name: Sheriff Michelle Valenti
characters.description: Connected All Along: As a young deputy, she was the one who responded toMax, Michael, and Isobel being found abandoned at age 7. She also did a great deal of the follow-up work on their case, so she knows better than anyone how inexplicable their sudden appearance really was. Da Chief: She's Max and Cam's boss; true to this trope, she's occasionally shown performing the political side of her job, like reassuring prominent citizens that their concerns are heard. Reasonable Authority Figure: She and her family are devoted to law and order, though she's not such aBy-the-Book Copthat she won't bend the occasional rule. Secret Chaser: In season 2 especially. She's aware that Max is hiding something; she's partially but not completely right about what he's hiding. The Sheriff: The modern-day version; she's the chief law enforcement officer for the county.

characters.name: MimiDeLuca
characters.description: Aura Vision: How Mimi's clairvoyance works. The Mentally Disturbed: Mimi has moments of lucidity, but she's too mentally fragile to live on her own. Power Limiter: Her family necklace. Seers: She can see auras and gain insights into people. Uneven Hybrid:1/4 alien. Mimi's mother Patricia was half-alien.

characters.name: Rosa Ortecho
characters.description: Age-Appropriate Angst: Liz idolized her beloved big sister and wondered how Rosa could possibly make such disastrous choices—but Rosa was a scared kid in a very difficult situation who was masking insecurities with attitude. Back from the Dead:She's brought back by Max in Season 2. Broken Bird: Rosa struggled with untreated mental illness and addiction throughout her life. Came Back Strong:Max passed on a bit of hisShock and Awepowers when he resurrected her. Fish out of Temporal Water:She's adjusting to the present day after ten years dead.

characters.name: Jesse Manes
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He was emotionally and violently abusive to Alex, now that Alex is an adult the violence has stopped the emotional abuse is still very much present. His son Flint buys completely into his father's bigotry and seems to be the model son, but he privately admits to Alex he did it out of fear of their father's retribution, while his wife and oldest son Gregory outright fled the house. Bait the Dog: He has a number of sympathetic moments with his sons in season 2, which suggest that he might have regretted what he did to them and seeks to make amends.Nope. He's just using them and if anything he's gotten worse, as he's now willing to kill Alex. Dramatic Irony: Part of his reason for hating aliens is that he looked up to his uncle Tripp, who was murdered by one.His uncle was actually helping the aliens and tried to instill those same values in Jesse, but Jesse's father found out, killed him, and blamed it on the aliens. Hate Sink: Utterly lacking in redeeming qualities. Heteronormative Crusader: Just another check box on Jesse's list of bigotry targets. While he was abusive to his family in general, it was especially bad for Alex due to him being gay and his father being willing to attemptCure Your Gaysby beating him.

characters.name: Jones
characters.description: Abusive Parents:Nothing quite like introducing yourself to your son by trying to murder him. Not to mention all the emotional manipulation he puts Max, his clone, through. Beard of Evil: He's got a heavy beard from all that time spent alone. He eventually shaves it. Big Bad: Of Season 3. Engineered Heroics: He started the apocalypse that claimed his homeworld so that he could get the credit for becoming its savior. Faux Affably Evil: He's never anything less than polite, especially when he's threatening to murder someone or forcing them to work for him.

characters.name: Noah Bracken
characters.description: Affably Evil: He's well-mannered and engages in mostly civil conversations with the heroes. A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing:Known in Roswell for being a nice guy, to the point Max refers to him as a golden retriever or Mr. Congeniality, it certainly comes as a shock for the heroes when it turns out he's a far more sinister person than they could have ever imagined. And I Must Scream:He managed to escape being rounded up by the military after the crash and hid in his pod. However, because he was from a lower class, his pod suffered more damage than the ones the trio used, so while it helped him stay alive, he was conscious for the entirety of 50 years, feeling his body slowly decay and unable to escape the pod due to how weak he was. From Nobody to Nightmare:According to Jones, Noah was actually one of the weakest aliens, on top of being from the lower class but on Earth he managed to not only be part of a higher class, he was also able to gain much more control and power in his abilities. If I Can't Have You…:His reasoning when killing Rosa. He realized she was afraid of him, planning to escape him and in a fit of rage he murdered her.
